day_shape: 56 items: Trump rules out same-day strike on Iran but keeps option open with oil above $116, CENTCOM's Cooper visits Strait of Hormuz, Qatari mediators in Tehran, Iran claims US drone downed over Bandar Abbas, Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi missiles over Riyadh.

threads.label: US–Iran posture around Hormuz
threads.summary: Trump told media the US would not strike Iran on Sunday but did not rule out later action, while CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper visited the Strait of Hormuz and an F-35C operated from USS George Washington in the Arabian Sea. Jerusalem Post reported Qatari mediators arrived in Tehran in a US-coordinated de-escalation effort, and a separate report cited Iranian officials describing plots to target US diplomats.

threads.label: Iranian regime messaging on war and economy
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press ran items claiming arrests of a 'Zionist cyber network' in Hormozgan, downplaying a Tabriz blast as disposal of failed ammunition, and quoting the Foreign Ministry's Qanbari that sanctions failed to stop Iran's economy. IRIB also claimed the Iranian army shot down a US drone over Bandar Abbas, and ran a cycle of smart-fuel-card statistics and Pezeshkian remarks on a registration-based census.

threads.label: Yemen–Saudi exchanges
threads.summary: Iran International and Jerusalem Post reported the Saudi-led coalition intercepted Houthi drones and missiles over Riyadh and southern areas, and Pope Leo called for an end to the violence in Yemen. Defa Press and IRIB carried Ansarallah statements demanding Saudi Arabia end its blockade and warning passengers to avoid Saudi airports except Mecca and Medina.

threads.label: IDF Gaza and West Bank operations
threads.summary: The IDF said two operatives involved in funnelling millions of shekels from Iran and Turkey to Hamas were killed in strikes in Gaza City and Nuseirat last week, and announced a diverted strike on a Hamas target in Gaza City. Israeli police arrested three Hebron residents over social-media support for Friday's West Bank attack, and a former chief military prosecutor was named to lead the Nukhba prosecution.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressure and dissent
threads.summary: Iran International reported the judiciary indicted comedian Saeed Shakiba on charges including supporting Israel and the Pahlavi dynasty, and the head of Iran's Psychology and Counseling Organization warned the country was nearing a mental-health emergency. Jerusalem Post cited former Mossad chief David Barnea saying a published video was designed to trigger mass arrests and hinder IRGC identification of Israeli agents.
